technical-data.invention-title: FORMULATIONS SERVANT A REGULER LA CROISSANCE DE PLANTES

abstract.p: Plant growth regulation preparations comprising a) 0.1 to 20 % by weight of a 16,17-dihydro gibberrelin of general formulae (Ia) or (Ib); b) up to 99.9 % by weight of a formulation additive selected from the group consisting of b1) the reaction products of triglycerides based on carboxylic acids having 2 to 30 carbon atoms and ethylene oxide and/or propylene oxide in the presence of a base, and/or b2) fatty acid esters of sugar alcohol polyethoxylates; c) up to 50 % by weight of an organic solvent; d) 0.1 to 50 % by weight of a formulation auxiliary different from b1 and b2; e) up to 50 % by weight of additional plant growth regulating compounds.

Préparations servant à réguler la croissance de plantes et contenant: (a) 0,1 à 20 % en poids de 16, 17-dihydrogiberreline représentée par les formules (Ia) ou (Ib); (b) 99,9 % en poids maximum d'un additif de formulation sélectionné dans le groupe constitué par :(b1) les produits réactionnels de triglycérides basés sur des acides carboxyliques possédant 2 à 30 atomes de carbone et oxyde d'éthylène et/ou de propylène en présence d'une base et/ou (b2) des esters d'acides gras de polyéthoxylates d'alcool de sucre; (c) 50 % en poids maximum d'un solvant organique; (d) 0,1 à 50 % en poids d'un adjuvant de formulation différent de b1 et b2; (e) 50 % en poids maximum de composés supplémentaires de régulation de la croissance de plantes.

description.p: Plant growth regulating formulations
The present invention relates to plant growth regulating preparations comprising
a) 0.1 to 20 % by weight of a 16 , 17-dihydro gibberrelin of general formulae la or lb
b) up to 99.9 % by weight of an formulation additive selected from the group consisting of
bl) the reaction products of triglycerides based on carboxylic acids having 2 to 30 carbon atoms and ethylene oxide and/or propylene oxide in the presence of a base, and/or
b2) fatty acid esters of sugar alcohol polyethoxylates
c) up to 50 % by weight of an organic solvent
d) 0.1 to 50 % by weight of a formulation auxiliary different from bl and b2 ,
e) up to 50 % by weight of additional plant growth regulating compounds.
Furthermore, the present invention relates to the use of the said preparations for the regulation of plant growth.

Numerous plant growth substances are known. Part of these substances are used in agriculture and horticulture in order to induce desired effects, for instance on seed germination and seedling growth rooting • dormancy juvenility, maturity and senescence flowering abscission of leaves, flowers and fruits fruit set and development • tuber formation growth of shoot and root photoassimilation control of unwanted plants senescence of whole plants or single organs

[cf. R. N. Arteca (1996) Plant Growth Substances, Chapman & Hall, New York . ]
Gibberellins (GAs) represent one group of plant growth substances. GAs occur naturally in higher plants where they function as phytohormones being involved in the regulation of growth and flowering and numerous other developmental 5 processes. Certain GAs, particularly gibberellic acid or GA3 (ent-3α, 10, 13-trihydroxy-20-norgiberrell-l , 16-diene-7 , 19-dioic acid 19 , 10-lactone) , are commercially available as fermentation products of the fungus Gibberella fuj ikuroi .

10 C-16 , 17-dihydro GAs and related structures have been known since many years. They either occur naturally in higher plants (e.g. GAs2 and and GAs ) or in the fungi Gibberella fuj ikuroi (e.g. GA2, GAio, GA42) and Phaeospheria sp . (e.g. GAs2) •

15 WO 93/03616 and PCT/AU95/000528 describe for the first time the biological activity of known and newly synthesized 16 , 17-dihydro GAs and their potential utility for agricultural, horticultural and plant breeding applications. In particular the following biological effects have been described as features of the
20 16 , 17-dihydro GAs and/or other ring D-modified GAs:
• dwarfing
• growth retardation of stem and shoot and/or root
• promotion of bud break
• flowering
25 • improved fruit quality
• inhibition of fruit ripening
• prevention of whole plant and/or organ senescence
• improved fruit set
• control of weed growth 30 • inducing male sterility
• retarded bud break
• tillering
Further details on chemical and biological aspects of distinct 35 16 , 17-dihydro or other ring D-modified GAs have been published in the recent scientific literature.
A major obstacle to introduce the ring D-modified gibberellin derivatives described in WO 93/03616 and PCT/AU95/00528 into

40 agricultural and horticultural practice is caused by the costs required to produce these compounds. The production costs are primarily affected by the price of the starting material GA3 [cf. W. Rademacher (1997): Gibberellins, in Fungal Biotechnology, T. Anke (ed. ) , Chapman & Hall, Weinheim, pp. 193-205].

45
There thus exists a need m formulations based on ring modified D-gibberelin derivatives having improved biologicasl activity and thus better economical feasibility.

The object of the present invention was to provide plant growth regulating preparations based on ring D-modified gibberellm derivatives having a very good biological activity, m particular at low application rates.
This obiect has been achieved with the plant growth regulating formulations as defined m claim 1 and hereinbefore.
Preferred embodiments of the instant invention are set forth m the dependent claims and the following detailed specification.

The component bl is obtainable by the reaction of an oil/fat based on a triglyceride of carboxylic acids having 2 to 30 carbon atoms and ethylene oxide and/or propylene oxide m the presence of a base. Fatty acid alkoxylates are primarily formed.
In the triglyceπdes , three equivalents of carboxylic acid are esterified with glycerol . The carboxylic acids can be saturated or mono- or polyethylenically unsaturated.
Preferably, the present invention uses naturally occurring oils and fats which contain tπglycerides as the main constituent. They can be crude, denatured or refined.

Suitable natural oils and fats are: vegetable oils such as olive oil, safflower oil, soybean oil, groundnut oil, cotton oil, corn oil, rape oil, castor oil, sunflower oil, coffee oil, linseed oil, coconut fat and mixtures thereof, animal fats and oils such as fish oils, e.g. sardine oil, herring oil, salmon oil, shark-liver oil or whale oil, and further tallow oil, bone oil, woolfat fractions and bovine tallow.
The following vegetable oils are preferred: castor oil, soybean oil, rape oil and corn oil. Particularly preferred of these is castor oil.
5 Per mol of the triglyceride on which the oil is based, from 1 to 100, preferably from 10 to 35 and m particular from 15 to 30, mol of ethylene oxide and/or propylene oxide are employed.

Suitable bases are especially inorganic bases such as the alkali 10 metal or alkaline earth metal hydroxides, e.g. sodium hydroxide, potassium hydroxide or calcium hydroxide. Instead of the direct use of hydroxides, it is possible to use carbonates or hydro- talcites, which, if appropriate, were hydrophobized with aliphatic or aromatic carboxylic acids, alcohols having 4 to 15 22 carbon atoms or the ethoxylates of alcohols of this type, or basic alkaline earth metal phosphates such as strontium phosphate, barium phosphate and calcium pnosphate, each of which also form hydroxide ions m the presence of small amounts of water. 20
The base particularly used is potassium hydroxide.
Per mol of triglyceride, from 0.1 to 5, and m particular from 0.1 to 2 , % by weight of base, based on the weight of the 25 triglyceride, are generally added to the reaction mixture.
The reaction is generally carried out at elevated pressure, preferably at from 1 to 10 and m particular at from 1 to 5 bar and at from 80 to 230 and especially from 100 to 150°C. 30
Workmg-up is in general carried out such that excess ethylene oxide or propylene oxide is removed under reduced pressure.

Otherwise, the carrymg-out of such alkoxylation reactions and 35 the isolation of the resulting reaction products is known to the person skilled m the art (cf. N. Schonfeldt, Grenzflachenaktive Ethylenoxidaddukte [Surface-active ethylene oxide adducts] , Wissenschaf tliche Verlagsgesellschaft mbH, Stuttgart, 1984) .

40 A particularly preferred product for component bl is the product obtainable by the reaction of an oil/fat based on a triglyceride of carboxylic acids having 10 to 20 carbon atoms and 10 to 30 mol equivalents of ethylene oxide and/or propylene oxide m the presence of hydroxide ions.

45
Preferred as component b2 are the esters derived from C8-C28 fatty acids with C5- and/or C6 sugar alcohol polyethoxylates comprising preferably of from 10 to 100, particularly 20 to 50 ethoxylate units .
Preferred fatty acids are oleic acid, steaπc acid, pelargomc acid and 2-Ethylhexanoιc acid or mixtures thereof.
Component b can be solely constituted of component bl or b2 or of mixtures of both species.
Component b constitutes up to 99.9, preferably 0.5 to 50, m particular 0.5 to 25 % by weight of the formulations m accordance with the instant invention.
The formulations according to the invention can moreover additionally contain further customary additives such as surfactants, antifoams, cosolvents, etc.
Suitable surfactants are:

anionic surfactants, e.g. alkali metal, alkaline earth metal or ammonium salts of the fatty acids such as potassium stearate, alkylsulfates , alkyl ether sulfates, alkyl- or lsoalkylsulfonates , alkylbenzenesulfonates such as Na dodecylbenzenesulfonates , alkylnaphthalenesulfonates , alkylmethyl ester sulfonates, acylglutamates , alkylsuccimc acid ester sulfonates, sarcosinates such as sodium lauroyl sarcosmate or taurates ,
cationic surfactants, e.g. alkyltrimethylammonium halides or alkylsulfates , alkylpyridimum halides or dialkyldimethy lammonium halides or alkylsulfates ,

- nonionic surfactants, e.g. alkoxylated animal or vegetable fats and oils such as corn oil ethoxylates, castor oil ethoxylates, tallow fat ethoxylates, glycerol esters such as glycerol monostearate, fatty alcohol alkoxylates and oxo- alcohol alkoxylates, fatty acid alkoxylates such as oleic acid ethoxylates, alkylphenyl alkoxylates such as lsononyl- phenol ethoxylates, fatty amme alkoxylates, fatty acid amide alkoxylates, sugar surfactants such as sorbitan fatty acid esters (sorbitan monooleate, sorbitan tristearate) , polyoxy ethylenesorbitan fatty acid esters, alkyl polyglycosides , N-alkylgluconamides, alkylmethyl sulfoxides, alkyldimethyl - phosphme oxides such as tetradecyldimethylphosphme oxide,
zwitteriomc surfactants, e.g. sulfobetames , carboxy betames, alkyldimethylamme oxides such as tetradecyl- dimethylamme oxide,

- polymer surfactants, e.g. di-, tπ- or multi-blockpolymers of the type (AB)X, ABA and BAB such as polyethylene oxide- block-polypropylene oxide, polystyrene-block-polyethylene oxide, AB comb polymers such as polymethacrylate or poly- acrylate comb-polyethylene oxide,

perfluoro surfactants, silicone surfactants, phospholipids such as lecithin, ammo acid surfactants such as N-lauroyl gluta ate, surface-active homo- and copolymers such as polyvmylpyrrolidone, polyacrylic acid, polyvinyl alcohol, polyethylene oxide, maleic anhydπde-isobutene copolymers, vmylpyrrolidone-vinyl acetate copolymers.

Preferably, the surfactant used is one or more homogeneous or mixed esters of phosphoric acid or diphosphoric acid with poly- alkylene oxide ethers, the polyalkylene oxide ethers generally having only a single hydroxyl group (e.g. Klearfac©, manufacturer: BASF Corp.).

Suitable polyalkylene oxide ethers are, for example, ethers of alkylphenols such as nonylphenol or of branched or unbranched aliphatic alcohols, for example having 6 to 30, preferably having 10 to 20, carbon atoms and in particular of fatty alcohols having 10 to 12 carbon atoms.

The monohydroxylateα polyalkylene oxide ethers are generally known or accessible in a manner known per se, especially by alkoxylation of the corresponding alcohols. Preferred alkoxylatmg agents are ethylene oxide and propylene oxide, which can be reacted with a suitable phosphorus compound individually, a mixture, succession or alternately, by means of which alkoxylation products of differing composition, for example having block structures, can result.

The preparation of these phosphoric acid esters is generally known and is carried out, for example, by reaction of the corresponding monofunctional polyalkylene oxide ether with phosphoric acid, d phospnorus pentoxide, polyphosphoπc acid or phosphorus oxytrichloπde (cf. "Nomonic Surfactants", Martin Schick (Ed.), Marcel Dekker, New York, 1964, Chapter 11, pages 372 - 394) .
The proportion of the surfactants can be from 0 to 30, preferably from 2 to 15, % by weight.
Suitable antifoams are aliphatic or aromatic monoalcohols having 4 to 14, preferably 6 to 10, carbon atoms, such as n-octanol or n-decanol or siiicone surfactants.
The proportion of the antifoams m the mixture is normally from 0.5 to 15 and especially from 3 to 8 % by weight.

Suitable cosolvents are mineral oils, naturally occurring oils such as rape oil, soybean oil and the methyl esters of carboxylic acids on which these oils are based, such as methyl oleate and rape oil methyl ester, fatty acid esters, especially with Cι_-C4-alkanols and organic solvents such as benzenes or naphthalenes substituted by straight-chain or branched alkyl groups (Shellsol 150®, Shellsol 200® and Solvesso® brands).
The proportion of the cosolvents m the mixture can be from 1 to 60 and especially from 5 to 30 % by weight.
Furthermore, the mixture can contain from 0 to 15 and especially from 2 to 10 % by weight of water.

Additionally, the mixture can contain one or more carboxylic acids having from 4 to 20, in particular from 6 to 18, carbon atoms such as oleic acid or 2-ethylhexanoιc acid and/or one or more of the dicarboxylic acids on whicn the compounds I are based, e.g. adipic acid, sebacic acid or succinic acid.
The proportion of these (di) carboxylic acids m the mixture is from 0 to 30, preferably from 0 to 10, % by weight.
As component d) the plant growth regulating formulations accordance with the instant invention can additionally contain further known plant growth regulating compounds.

The biological activity of 16 , 17-dihydro GAs can be improved a synergistic manner (cf. S.R. Colby, Weeds 25: 20-22) by co-applying them with other plant growth regulators. This is particularly observed when using the preferred compounds VI or VII formulations or spray solutions m combination with other growth retardants, I. e. compounds leading to a reduction of shoot length. Plant growth retardants of practical relevance are, for instance, ethephon (standard compound I) , the quaternary ammonium compounds chlormequat chloride (standard compound II) - mepiquat chloride (standard compound III) , compounds possessing a N-contammg heterocycle ancymidol f lurpπmidol paclobutrazol - uniconazole-P abenfide, the acylcyclohexanediones prohexadione-Ca (standard compound IV) tr exapac-ethyl (standard compound V)

16 , 17-dihydro GAs are also suitable to synergize the biological activity of exogenously applied gibberellins, such as gibberellic acid (GA3 = standard compound VI) or other GAs with immediate biological activity (e.g. GA4 , GA ) . The commercially available GA3 and GA4+7 have found a large number of applications [for details see Thomson, W.H. (1995) Agricultural Chemicals, Book III, Thomson Publications, Fresno, USA, p. 29-35].

Particularly m graminaceous species, the preferred compounds VI and VII synergize the action of exogenously applied GAs and can, thus, be used to increase the yield of malt and decrease the amount of time required for the malting process in the brewing industry increase the yield of sugar cane - stimulate germination and seedling development m rice, wheat, barley, oats, rye, maize, sorghum, turf grasses and other plant species.

In addition to enhancing the biological performance of 16,17-dι hydro-GAs by using suitable adjuvants for the preparation of formulations, additional optimisation can be achieved by adding further adjuvants to the spray solution (tank mixing) . Particularly preferred adjuvants are ammonium sulphate or citric acid added at a concentration of from 0.01 to 0.5 % by weight, preferably 0.05 to 0.2 % by weight.
Examples

Unless otherwise noted, the growth regulating proerties of different compounds m different formulations were determined under greenhouse conditions as follows:
Test plants were grown m plastic pots of approximately 12.5 cm m diameter m a substrate provided with sufficient nutrients and water. At an appropriate shoot length the plants were treated with aqueous sprays of the formulations. The growth-regulatmg action observed was confirmed at the end of the experiment by measuring the height of the plants. The results obtained were compared with the growth height of the untreated plants.

In cases m which a reduction growth height was achieved, a deeper leaf coloration could be observed. The increased chloro phyll content is indicative of an increased rate of photosynthesis, making for bigger yields.
